info.title: kestrel operator
info.summary: The boundary a Client reaches a control plane over.
info.description: Server-sent events down, JSON up, plain HTTP. It authenticates nobody, so the control plane serves it on a listener of its own, apart from the link, and binds that listener to loopback unless told otherwise. A remote control plane is reached through a tunnel. Every operation refuses with 403, and does nothing, a request whose Host is not loopback, or whose Origin, when it sends one, is not exactly http:// followed by that Host.

get.description: Asked of the Instance's supervisor over the link and answered live; never written to the Store, Transcript or Event log. Each entry is marked tracked, untracked or ignored. A directory past 5,000 entries is truncated, and `total` says how many it holds. Symlinks are resolved, and a path outside the Workspace's checkouts is refused. Concurrent identical reads share one request, and an answer is reused for about 5 s.

A binary file, a file past 1 MiB, or a `raw` read is streamed as `application/octet-stream`, unbuffered and with no cap, and never shared or cached. Symlinks are resolved, and a path outside the Workspace's checkouts is refused.

get.summary: Read the Organization's queue: the limits, their occupancy, the queued Sessions in dispatch order, the Waiting Sessions and the unbriefed ones.
get.description: Queued Sessions appear in the order they were enqueued. Each one ready for dispatch apart from the shared Active-Work Slot pool is numbered from 1; one that is not carries no number and names every reason that holds it, derived by the rules dispatch applies. A queued Session whose Workspace has no Brief waits only on its Instance. Waiting Sessions follow, unnumbered, with any held input and why their next turn has not started. Unbriefed Sessions follow those, beside them: they hold their Instances and no Active-Work Slot, are never numbered, and carry the step they are preparing on and any message held for their Brief. Nothing is estimated. The Active-Work Slot limit and the Compute driver are the ones the dispatching work role recorded, or no work role is dispatching; the pool belongs to the control plane and every Organization shares it, so other Organizations' occupants are counted and never named. Reading changes nothing.

get.summary: Stream a Workspace's Transcript.
get.description: Replays every entry after `Last-Event-ID`, in order, each as an `entry` event whose id is the cursor that resumes after it. A read that follows then stays open and delivers entries as they are appended; the stream ends with an `end` event once the Workspace is sealed, or at once for a read that does not follow. A cursor that names no position in this Transcript is refused rather than silently restarting the walk. A follow that stays open past caught-up registers a follower: it is sent one `follower` event carrying its id and lease, then a `presence` event carrying the whole current set, and a new `presence` event whenever the set changes. Presence events carry no id and never move the cursor, and a read that does not follow registers nobody.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: The Workspace whose Transcript is read, by its generated name, its identifier, any unambiguous prefix of its identifier, or `latest`.

parameters.name: follow
parameters.description: Whether to stay open for entries appended after the ones already recorded.

parameters.name: as
parameters.description: The person this follow joins the Workspace's presence as, by the participant name rule; naming an Agent in the Organization is refused. Only a read that stays open past caught-up registers a follower.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The id of the last entry this reader was delivered. Absent means from the beginning.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.description: Comma-separated Transcript kinds. The cursor advances across every examined seq, including omitted kinds.

parameters.name: summaries
parameters.description: Summarize omitted narration and detail, across every shared-state boundary even when shared state is not selected. With every kind selected there are no summaries.

parameters.name: first_seq
parameters.description: Inclusive first seq of an Activity expansion. Select every kind to read its entries.

parameters.name: last_seq
parameters.description: Inclusive last seq of an Activity expansion; must be at least first_seq. The finite range ends when caught up.

200.description: The stream is open. Each event carries an entry, the end of the stream, a follower registration or the whole presence set as its data, and its name as its event name.

parameters.name: id

get.summary: Stream the Organization's change notices.
get.description: Opens with an `open` event, then sends a `change` event naming each Workspace, Session or queue that changed, at most once per resource per 250 ms. A notice says what changed, never what it changed to. No event carries an id and `Last-Event-ID` is ignored: a notice is a hint to refetch, never a cursor. A subscriber that falls behind the bounded buffer is sent `resync` instead of a silent gap.

200.description: The stream is open. `open` and `resync` mean every subscribed view must be refetched; `change` names one resource.

Refused.description: The control plane refused the request. 400 is a request it could not read; 403 is a name that is not the one the change requires; 404 is a name or reference that resolves to no record, or to more than one; 409 and 422 are an operation it declined; 503 is a control plane that could not answer; 504 is an Instance that did not answer a read within 10 s.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before asking again. Present on a 503 only when the database was busy, which asking again can clear.

PayloadReference.description: A body field exceeding 65536 bytes, fetched under its owning Workspace; message, thought and brief text use raw UTF-8, while plans, batched messages and tool input/results use compact JSON.

preparing.description: The step an unbriefed Session is preparing on: provisioning from claim until its supervisor connects, cloning until its checkout is reported, starting_harness until the harness is up, and harness_ready once it is. Null in every other state.

model.description: What the Session names for its Harness's model, or null for its Harness's default.

mode.description: What the Session names for its Harness's mode, or null for its Harness's default.

thought_level.description: What the Session names for its Harness's thought level, or null for its Harness's default.

worked_model.description: The Model-category option's current value, kept current by the supervisor (ADR-0041).

title.description: The harness's own name for the conversation, or null until it says one.

changing_options.description: Option changes a person asked for while the Session is live, held until the harness answers each (ADR-0041).

commands.description: The commands the harness offers for this Session.

interrupting.description: Who asked the working Turn to stop, while the request is in flight.

units.description: Adapter units still running, such as a Claude background task; they keep a trailing Session trailing.

last_activity_at.description: When the trailing Session's agent last showed activity; null in every other state.

SessionOption.description: A harness config option, whole: what it is, what it may be and what it is now.

category.description: `mode`, `model`, `model_config`, `thought_level`, or the harness's own string, which may begin with `_`.

current.description: The current value: a value id for a select, a boolean for a toggle.

values.description: The offered values of an ungrouped select; empty for a grouped one and for a boolean.

groups.description: The offered values of a grouped select; empty for an ungrouped one.

warns_cache.description: Whether changing this option makes the next Turn re-read the context without the prompt cache. True for a Model, ThoughtLevel or ModelConfig option, except a category kestrel's per-harness table keeps the cache for; at 0.3 that is Claude's ThoughtLevel (ADR-0041).

SessionCommand.description: A command the harness offers for the Session, as a composer lists it.

Interrupting.description: A person's request that a Session's working Turn stop.

participant.description: The person asking. Trimmed, 1 to 64 characters with no control characters, and never the name of an Agent in the Organization.

ProviderCredential.description: A credential as everything but the Session that carries it sees it.

owner.description: The person it belongs to, which never changes.

SubscriptionProfileLogin.description: A login as everything but the Session that carries it sees it.

name.description: The variable, or the path beneath the agent's home.

set_at.description: When it was last held, whether by a person or by a Session handing back a refreshed login.

IntegrationRegistration.description: A registration, by the kind of external system it connects to.

GithubRegistration.description: A connection to GitHub, watching one repository.

repository.description: The repository it watches, as owner/name.

token.description: The credential it presents to GitHub.

carries.description: The directions it carries. Absent means both.

interval.description: How often the poll asks GitHub what has happened, as a duration such as `1m` or `PT30S`.

webhook_secret.description: The secret GitHub signs webhook deliveries with. Given one, the repository's events arrive by webhook and it is not polled.

WebhookRegistration.description: A generic endpoint any producer can POST CloudEvents to. It carries inbound only.

secret.description: The secret a sender presents as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`.

carries.description: The directions it carries. Absent means inbound.

Integration.description: A registered Integration. What it presents to the external system is never part of it.

repository.description: The repository a GitHub Integration watches.

polled_every.description: How often it is polled, when it is.

webhook_path.description: Where on the link its events are delivered, when they are delivered rather than polled.

EventRefusal.description: The latest Event an Integration refused rather than stored, visible until acknowledged.

EventRecord.description: An Event as kestrel recorded it.

record.description: kestrel's own identifier for the record.

integration.description: The Integration that recorded it. Null for an Event kestrel minted itself.

firings.description: What each Trigger that matched it did, oldest first.

Firing.description: One Trigger matching the Event, and what that match did.

workspace.description: The Workspace it opened or fed.

failure.description: Why a failed firing started nothing, such as labels choosing two Agents.

CloudEvent.description: The Event's CloudEvents envelope and payload.

Activity.description: Read-time summary of omitted narration and detail between consecutive shared-state entries. first_seq identifies the whole Activity, including selected kinds, and stays stable across pages and reconnects. last_seq is the highest Activity seq examined; its SSE id advances the global cursor. A closed replacement precedes the closing shared-state entry even when no detail was added. No summary is stored.

started_at.description: Earliest start among omitted unexpired entries.

finished_at.description: Latest finish among omitted unexpired entries.

anomaly.description: An omitted call was interrupted or unresolved.

closed.description: The next shared-state boundary has been examined. Followers replace open summaries by first_seq and CLI followers print only this final replacement.

Recorded.description: One Transcript entry, and where it sits in the order.

ExpiredEntry.description: Narration or detail expired in place after 30 days from append, including in sealed Workspaces. The enclosing record retains its original kind, seq and appended_at, with session_id null; all content, completion metadata and payload references are removed.

expired_at.description: When the sweep replaced the entry.

Entry.description: One completed unit of the Workspace Transcript.

Brief.description: The instruction a Workspace started with, rendered by the Trigger that fired or supplied by an operator.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

BriefSource.description: Who supplied a Brief: the Trigger whose firing rendered it, or an operator, under the participant name they declared if they declared one.

participant.description: The participant who joined directly before the Brief, or null when the operator declared no name and no one joined.

SessionStarted.description: A Session started on behalf of the Workspace.

Messages.description: Messages that arrived while a Session was active, drained as one Transcript entry.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

SpokenMessage.description: One Participant's message within a drained group.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

SessionEnded.description: A Session ended, and how it went.

TurnInterrupted.description: A person interrupted a working Turn without ending the Session.

because.description: Why it failed. Absent when it succeeded.

field.description: The request field the message concerns, when the refusal is about one.

End.description: The control plane closed the stream on purpose. A stream that closes without one was cut off, and is resumed from the last id delivered.

because.description: `caught_up` when a read that does not follow has delivered every entry; `sealed` when the Workspace is sealed and every entry it will ever hold has been delivered.

TranscriptSessionState.description: Transient session_state SSE snapshot on every follow connect, including empty state, then changes. Never has an event id and never enters the Transcript. session_id is null when no unfinished Session exists; usage is the latest the Harness reported, live, or null.

usage.description: What the Harness has spent so far, kept in memory while the Session is live; null until it reports one.

last_activity_at.description: When the agent last showed activity, present only while its Session trails its answer.

Event.description: SSE names: entry (Recorded), activity (Activity), session_state (TranscriptSessionState), cursor (CursorEvent), end (End), follower (FollowerEvent), or presence (Presence). Entry, Activity and cursor IDs advance the global Transcript cursor; session_state, follower and presence carry no id. Activity replacements retain first_seq, and their final closed replacement precedes the closing shared-state entry.

FollowerEvent.description: A follow that stayed open past caught-up registered: the id it renews by, and the lease in seconds it must renew before. Sent once per follow.

Presence.description: The whole current set of a Workspace's followers, sent when a follow registers and whenever the set changes. A named follow appears once per name, the follower's own included; unnamed follows are counted; an Agent never appears. Carries no Transcript cursor.

OptionChangedEntry.description: A person changed one of a Session's options between Turns (ADR-0041).

participant.description: The person who made the change.

option.description: The harness option's id, or the category when a queued Session's declared value changed.

from.description: What the option was set to before the change.

to.description: What it was set to; null when the harness refused.

refused.description: Why the harness refused, when it did.

PullRequestEntry.description: A verified GitHub Event observed a pull request from the Workspace's declared branch in one of its repositories. Learning it starts no work.

event.description: The Organization Event it was learned from.

repository.description: The head repository fixed on the Workspace.

InstanceReleased.description: A person released the Workspace's Instance, destroying it and whatever it held that was never pushed.

unpublished.description: What it held that existed nowhere else, as judged when it was released; null when it held nothing.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.
Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

CursorEvent.description: A cursor event carries the highest examined workspace:seq as its SSE id and data, so a filtered read resumes beyond omitted entries.

status.description: The status the Harness last reported for the call.

input.description: Inline JSON, or a PayloadReference when the serialized value exceeds 65536 bytes.

result.description: Inline JSON, or a PayloadReference when the serialized value exceeds 65536 bytes.

closing_reason.description: Why kestrel closed the call at a Turn boundary; null when the Harness settled it.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

RunningUnit.description: Work an adapter declared it runs apart from any tool call, such as a Claude background task, open until the adapter settles it. A settled unit adds no Transcript entry.

ChangesEvent.description: SSE names: open (Refetch) on connect and on reconnect, change (Change) for one resource that changed, and resync (Refetch) for a subscriber that fell behind the bounded buffer. No event carries an id.

Change.description: One resource that changed: a Workspace or Session by id, with the name of the Workspace it belongs to, or the Organization's queue, which carries neither. Never a copy of its state.

workspace.description: The name of the Workspace that holds the Session.

Refetch.description: The event that means refetch every view the Client subscribes to. It carries no fields.
